slides.title: A client scheduled for ECT tomorrow asks, “Can I refuse the ECT treatment tomorr
text: Question: A client scheduled for ECT tomorrow asks, “Can I refuse the ECT treatment tomorrow?” Which response should the nurse make?
A. “You should consider discussing this decision with your family first.”
B. “Having this treatment can be scary, but it is going to help you feel better.”
C. “Let’s talk with your doctor before you make a final decision.”
D. “You have a right to refuse even though you have signed the consent.”
Correct answer: D. “You have a right to refuse even though you have signed the consent.”
Topic: Legal, Ethics & Management
notes: Rationale:
Clients can withdraw consent at any time. The nurse is a client advocate and must not coerce, reassure falsely, or delay the client’s decision.

slides.title: Which statement indicates correct understanding of informed consent?
text: Question: Which statement indicates correct understanding of informed consent?
A. It is an agreement to receive medical treatment that cannot be revoked once signed.
B. Forms must be signed when a client is competent to make an informed decision.
C. It is signed by the nurse to indicate the client understands the procedure.
D. It is the nurse’s responsibility to explain the risks, benefits, and alternatives.
Correct answer: B. Forms must be signed when a client is competent to make an informed decision.
Topic: Legal, Ethics & Management
notes: Rationale:
The client must be competent (capacity) to consent, and consent can be revoked. The provider explains risks/benefits/alternatives, and the nurse only witnesses the signature.

slides.title: After change-of-shift report, the nurse should first see the client who
text: Question: After change-of-shift report, the nurse should first see the client who
A. had laparoscopic surgery 12 hours ago with right shoulder pain.
B. had a cardiac catheterization 1 hour ago and has been drowsy since the procedure.
C. is scheduled for an echocardiogram in 1 hour and is eating food from a visitor.
D. had an ERCP 1 hour ago and is reporting difficulty swallowing.
Correct answer: D. had an ERCP 1 hour ago and is reporting difficulty swallowing.
Topic: Prioritization & Delegation
notes: Rationale:

Difficulty swallowing after ERCP (sedation, throat anesthesia, or duodenal perforation) threatens the airway — ABCs. Referred shoulder pain after laparoscopy is expected, and a drowsy client after sedation is not unusual.

slides.title: In L&D, several clients are in second-stage labor on external monitors. Which cl
text: Question: In L&D, several clients are in second-stage labor on external monitors. Which client is a priority for follow-up?
A. Cervix dilated to 10 cm with moderately intense contractions of 40–50 seconds.
B. FHR consistent at 132 bpm.
C. Bloody show that is dark red with active pushing.
D. Contractions lasting 60 seconds with a 3-minute interval.
Correct answer: C. Bloody show that is dark red with active pushing.
Topic: Maternal-Newborn
notes: Rationale:
Bloody show should be pink or red-tinged mucus. Dark red bleeding could indicate abruptio placentae or uterine problems. The other findings are normal for second stage.

slides.title: The RN is assigning tasks. Which is best to assign to the LPN/VN?
text: Question: The RN is assigning tasks. Which is best to assign to the LPN/VN?
A. Collection of past medical history for a client admitted for cellulitis.
B. Recording output for a client who urinated in the toilet collection container.
C. Assisting with delivery of breakfast trays.
D. Developing a plan of care for a client postoperative from a cholecystectomy.
Correct answer: A. Collection of past medical history for a client admitted for cellulitis.
Topic: Prioritization & Delegation
notes: Rationale:
LPN/VNs may collect data and contribute to the plan of care. UAPs record output and deliver trays. The RN is responsible for developing the care plan.

slides.title: Which client information requires the ED nurse to report to an outside agency?
text: Question: Which client information requires the ED nurse to report to an outside agency?
A. 18-year-old at 4 months pregnant with abdominal pain.
B. 27-year-old with a history of gonorrhea and chlamydia from 1 year ago.
C. 45-year-old injured in a factory fire with 50% TBSA burns.
D. 72-year-old living with their daughter who has several stage 3 pressure ulcers.
Correct answer: D. 72-year-old living with their daughter who has several stage 3 pressure ulcers.
Topic: Legal, Ethics & Management
notes: Rationale:
Several stage 3 pressure ulcers in a dependent older adult suggest neglect/abuse, which is mandated reporting (Adult Protective Services). Past STIs aren’t reportable now.

slides.title: On the pediatric unit, which child should the nurse assess first?
text: Question: On the pediatric unit, which child should the nurse assess first?
A. 15-year-old with acute post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis and crackles with neck vein distention.
B. 13-year-old with hemophilia requiring prolonged pressure after a venipuncture.
C. 10-year-old with sickle cell disease reporting pain of 7/10 and due for pain medication.
D. 7-year-old with celiac disease and 3 episodes of diarrhea in 8 hours.
Correct answer: A. 15-year-old with acute post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis and crackles with neck vein distention.
Topic: Prioritization & Delegation
notes: Rationale:
Crackles and JVD signal fluid overload/heart failure and pulmonary edema in PSGN. This threatens breathing and needs immediate assessment. Others are expected or being managed.

slides.title: A client had a kidney transplant 1 week ago. It is a priority to notify the PHCP
text: Question: A client had a kidney transplant 1 week ago. It is a priority to notify the PHCP if the client has
A. urine that continues to be slightly pink since surgery.
B. an increase in weight from 199 to 201 lb over 72 hours.
C. a BUN change from 10 to 16 mg/dL over 48 hours.
D. a BP change from 122/78 to 92/58 mm Hg over 4 hours.
Correct answer: D. a BP change from 122/78 to 92/58 mm Hg over 4 hours.
Topic: Renal, Fluids & Acid-Base
notes: Rationale:
A significant BP drop suggests hypovolemia, hemorrhage, or sepsis, which threatens graft perfusion. Pink urine is expected early after surgery, and a 2 lb gain over 72 hours is minor.

slides.title: After assessing a newly admitted client with pericarditis, which action should t
text: Question: After assessing a newly admitted client with pericarditis, which action should the nurse take first when preparing the plan of care?
A. Prioritize the client’s reported concerns.
B. Determine any referrals that need to be initiated.
C. Formulate short-term and long-term goals.
D. Review client data to identify areas of concern.
Correct answer: D. Review client data to identify areas of concern.
Topic: Legal, Ethics & Management
notes: Rationale:
Nursing process: analyze the data first, identify the problems/nursing diagnoses, and then set priorities, goals, and interventions.

slides.title: Which documentation by a staff nurse indicates correct charting?
text: Question: Which documentation by a staff nurse indicates correct charting?
A. “IV site in antecubital space is red and warm. IV removed. New IV started.”
B. “Found client sitting on floor. Rails up. No pain. PHCP notified. Incident report completed.”
C. “Returned from radiology. VS obtained with slight increase in BP.”
D. “Ambulated from bed to doorway without assistance. No shortness of breath or diaphoresis noted. VS remain within baseline after ambulating.”
Correct answer: D. “Ambulated from bed to doorway without assistance. No shortness of breath or diaphoresis noted. VS remain within baseline after ambulating.”
Topic: Legal, Ethics & Management
notes: Rationale:
Good documentation is specific, objective, and measurable (activity, response, vitals). Avoid vague terms like “slight increase,” omitted details, and references to incident reports.

slides.title: Which situation requires the nurse to complete an incident report?
text: Question: Which situation requires the nurse to complete an incident report?
A. A client developed phlebitis from an IV catheter and is now receiving antibiotics.
B. A staff member called a code for a client in respiratory distress.
C. A client reports having an advance directive but has no copy on the chart.
D. The nurse finds a PRN prescription for restraints in the medical record.
Correct answer: A. A client developed phlebitis from an IV catheter and is now receiving antibiotics.
Topic: Legal, Ethics & Management
notes: Rationale:
Incident reports document unexpected events/adverse outcomes (e.g., IV complications requiring treatment). Calling a code is appropriate care, and the others are routine.

slides.title: A newly hired UAP is observed. Which action indicates correct client care?
text: Question: A newly hired UAP is observed. Which action indicates correct client care?
A. Donning sterile gloves to empty a urinary drainage device.
B. Removing protective eyewear before removing gloves.
C. Wearing a gown, mask, and gloves when entering the room of a client with influenza.
D. Placing dedicated equipment in the room of a client with cellulitis of the left leg.
Correct answer: C. Wearing a gown, mask, and gloves when entering the room of a client with influenza.
Topic: Infection Control & Safety
notes: Rationale:

Influenza requires droplet precautions (mask) plus standard precautions (gloves, gown if splash anticipated), so this is the only acceptable choice. Gloves come off first, and drainage emptying uses clean gloves.

slides.title: In an ambulatory center, which client should be removed from the waiting room im
text: Question: In an ambulatory center, which client should be removed from the waiting room immediately?
A. Reports burning and pruritus with a linear rash of vesicles around the right rib cage.
B. A 1 mm flat, red area at a Mantoux site given 48 hours ago.
C. Congestive heart failure and a 3 lb gain in 3 days.
D. Fever of 99.6° F, generalized pain, and borderline personality disorder.
Correct answer: A. Reports burning and pruritus with a linear rash of vesicles around the right rib cage.
Topic: Infection Control & Safety
notes: Rationale:
Herpes zoster (shingles) lesions are infectious to anyone without varicella immunity; place the client in an exam room under contact precautions.

slides.title: Which prescription should the nurse follow up on?
text: Question: Which prescription should the nurse follow up on?
A. Filgrastim for a client with WBC 2,500/mm³.
B. Preoperative atropine for a client with glaucoma.
C. Fluid bolus of 500 mL over 1 hour for a child in sickle cell crisis.
D. Low-potassium diet for a child with acute glomerulonephritis.
Correct answer: B. Preoperative atropine for a client with glaucoma.
Topic: Pharmacology & Labs
notes: Rationale:

Anticholinergics like atropine dilate the pupil and raise intraocular pressure (contraindicated in narrow-angle glaucoma). Filgrastim treats neutropenia, hydration helps sickle cell crisis, and K⁺ is restricted in AGN.

slides.title: A client postoperative from a colon resection arrives from the PACU, responds to
text: Question: A client postoperative from a colon resection arrives from the PACU, responds to commands, and reports moderate pain. Which action should the nurse take first?
A. Confirm the client’s identity.
B. Assess the client’s surgical bandage.
C. Auscultate the client’s abdomen.
D. Evaluate the client’s vital signs.
Correct answer: A. Confirm the client’s identity.
Topic: Prioritization & Delegation
notes: Rationale:
On arrival, verify identity with two identifiers before any assessment or care (patient-safety first); then assess ABCs/vitals, and so on. (Marked with a “?” on your copy.)

slides.title: The nurse is caring for a newborn with hyperbilirubinemia receiving phototherapy
text: Question: The nurse is caring for a newborn with hyperbilirubinemia receiving phototherapy. Which intervention should be included?
A. Cover the newborn with a light blanket.
B. Maintain the newborn on their back.
C. Remove the eye shields each shift or during feedings.
D. Provide a quiet, stimulus-free environment.
Correct answer: C. Remove the eye shields each shift or during feedings.
Topic: Maternal-Newborn
notes: Rationale:
Eye shields protect the retinas but are removed during feeding/each shift to assess the eyes and promote bonding. Expose maximum skin (no blankets) and reposition regularly.

slides.title: Which finding indicates a developmental delay?
text: Question: Which finding indicates a developmental delay?
A. 1-month-old who does not have head control.
B. 3-month-old who is unable to grasp objects.
C. 9-month-old who is unsteady when standing.
D. 14-month-old who is unable to drink from a cup.
Correct answer: D. 14-month-old who is unable to drink from a cup.
Topic: Pediatrics
notes: Rationale:
By about 12–15 months toddlers can drink from a cup. Lack of head control is expected at 1 month, voluntary grasp appears ~4–5 months, and standing unsteadily at 9 months is normal.

slides.title: LMP began August 26. Using Naegele’s rule, what is the EDD?
text: Question: LMP began August 26. Using Naegele’s rule, what is the EDD?
A. May 19
B. May 26
C. June 2
D. June 9
Correct answer: C. June 2
Topic: Maternal-Newborn
notes: Rationale:
Add 7 days → September 2; subtract 3 months → June 2.

slides.title: A client with breast cancer had a mastectomy and is receiving chemotherapy. Whic
text: Question: A client with breast cancer had a mastectomy and is receiving chemotherapy. Which statement indicates effective coping?
A. “I am glad the nausea and vomiting are subsiding.”
B. “I do not need as much pain medication as prescribed.”
C. “I made an appointment to get fitted for a prosthesis.”
D. “I will begin the next round of chemotherapy next week.”
Correct answer: C. “I made an appointment to get fitted for a prosthesis.”
Topic: Oncology & Radiation
notes: Rationale:
Taking active steps toward adapting to body-image change shows effective coping. The other statements are only observations of symptoms/treatment.

slides.title: A client with paranoid schizophrenia has lost 15 lb in 3 weeks and accuses staff
text: Question: A client with paranoid schizophrenia has lost 15 lb in 3 weeks and accuses staff of trying to poison them. Which intervention is a priority?
A. Ask the client what foods they would like to eat.
B. Allow the client to observe how the food is prepared.
C. Provide the client with prepackaged foods that they like.
D. Offer to sit with the client during meals.
Correct answer: C. Provide the client with prepackaged foods that they like.
Topic: Mental Health
notes: Rationale:
Individually packaged foods the client can open themselves reduce suspicion of tampering, so the client can eat safely and gain weight.

slides.title: A newly admitted client has major depressive disorder after the death of her new
text: Question: A newly admitted client has major depressive disorder after the death of her newborn 2 weeks ago. Which goal is the priority?
A. Signing a no-harm contract.
B. Exhibiting expected grieving behaviors.
C. Identifying positive qualities about herself.
D. Assuming an active role in the care planning process.
Correct answer: A. Signing a no-harm contract.
Topic: Mental Health
notes: Rationale:
Safety is the priority in depression with a major loss. Address suicide risk first; grieving, self-esteem, and participation come after.

slides.title: A home health nurse is talking to the spouse of a client receiving intermittent
text: Question: A home health nurse is talking to the spouse of a client receiving intermittent PEG tube feedings. Which statement indicates correct understanding?
A. “I check placement by checking gastric pH before each feeding.”
B. “I make sure my spouse sits up for at least an hour after the feeding.”
C. “I clean the reusable feeding system with soap and hot water every 48 hours.”
D. “I withhold the feeding if the gastric residual is 50 mL.”
Correct answer: B. “I make sure my spouse sits up for at least an hour after the feeding.”
Topic: GI & Nutrition
notes: Rationale:

Remain upright for 30–60 minutes after feeding to prevent aspiration. Home PEG placement isn’t checked with pH, systems are washed after each use, and residual thresholds are higher (typically hold at ≥250 mL in adults).

slides.title: A client on bed rest. Which action should the nurse take to help prevent venous
text: Question: A client on bed rest. Which action should the nurse take to help prevent venous thromboembolism?
A. Place the client on an alternating pressure relieving mattress.
B. Maintain the HOB at 60 degrees or higher.
C. Instruct the client to cough and deep breathe every hour.
D. Ensure the client maintains adequate hydration.
Correct answer: D. Ensure the client maintains adequate hydration.
Topic: Cardiovascular
notes: Rationale:
Hydration prevents hemoconcentration and venous stasis. Mattresses prevent pressure injuries, and coughing/deep breathing prevents atelectasis. (Also use SCDs, leg exercises and early ambulation.)

slides.title: The nurse is caring for a client in skeletal traction. Which action should the n
text: Question: The nurse is caring for a client in skeletal traction. Which action should the nurse take?
A. Maintain the bed in a reverse-Trendelenburg position.
B. Provide pin site care as prescribed.
C. Assess pedal push strength every 4 hours.
D. Turn the client to a 30-degree angle every 2 hours.
Correct answer: B. Provide pin site care as prescribed.
Topic: Neuro, Eyes & Ortho
notes: Rationale:
Skeletal traction uses pins through bone, with a high risk of osteomyelitis, so pin care is essential. The pulleys, ropes, and weights must hang freely.

slides.title: A client is 12 hours post TURP. Which should be in the plan of care?
text: Question: A client is 12 hours post TURP. Which should be in the plan of care?
A. Monitor hemoglobin and hematocrit levels.
B. Restrict oral fluids while receiving continuous bladder irrigation.
C. Notify the PHCP if the client has blood-tinged urine.
D. Perform intermittent irrigation of the catheter with sterile saline every hour.
Correct answer: A. Monitor hemoglobin and hematocrit levels.
Topic: Renal, Fluids & Acid-Base
notes: Rationale:
Hemorrhage is the main complication after TURP. Pink-tinged urine is expected, fluids are encouraged to flush the bladder, and CBI is continuous.

slides.title: A young adult female is newly prescribed carbamazepine for seizures. Which state
text: Question: A young adult female is newly prescribed carbamazepine for seizures. Which statement indicates correct understanding?
A. “I will weigh myself every week to check for weight gain.”
B. “If I want children, I should not delay starting a family.”
C. “I will use condoms as a method of birth control.”
D. “A low-sodium diet will need to be followed while on this medication.”
Correct answer: C. “I will use condoms as a method of birth control.”
Topic: Pharmacology & Labs
notes: Rationale:
Carbamazepine induces liver enzymes and reduces hormonal contraceptive effectiveness, and it’s teratogenic. Also teach to report sore throat/bruising (agranulocytosis).

Conflicting answer: the same question in the outside (not Galen) set "Comp 203 (set 2)" gives a different answer: "If I want children, I should not delay starting a family". Yours here is "“I will use condoms as a method of birth control.”". The two keys cannot both be what your instructor wants; check this one against your class materials.

slides.title: A client receiving epoetin alfa. Which finding indicates a therapeutic response?
text: Question: A client receiving epoetin alfa. Which finding indicates a therapeutic response?
A. WBC increased from 3,200 to 6,000/mm³.
B. Platelets increased from 115,000 to 145,000/mm³.
C. Hemoglobin increased from 10 to 16 g/dL.
D. PT increased from 11 to 22 seconds.
Correct answer: C. Hemoglobin increased from 10 to 16 g/dL.
Topic: Pharmacology & Labs
notes: Rationale:
Epoetin stimulates RBC production, so Hgb/Hct rise. (Target Hgb is usually ≤11–12 g/dL; excessive rise increases clot/stroke risk.) WBC suggests filgrastim, platelets suggest oprelvekin.

slides.title: IV morphine 1 mg every 2 hours is prescribed. Available: prefilled injectable 2
text: Question: IV morphine 1 mg every 2 hours is prescribed. Available: prefilled injectable 2 mg/mL. Which action should the nurse take?
A. Use a 1 mL syringe to remove 1 mg for later use.
B. Administer 1 mg and lock up the remaining 1 mg.
C. Have another nurse witness the waste of 1 mg from the prefilled injectable prior to administration.
D. Administer 1 mg and then have another nurse witness the waste of the remaining medication.
Correct answer: C. Have another nurse witness the waste of 1 mg from the prefilled injectable prior to administration.
Topic: Pharmacology & Labs
notes: Rationale:
Controlled substances must be wasted with a witness and documented; never save leftover opioid for later. Follow facility policy on the timing of the waste. (Your copy’s marked answer is C.)

slides.title: A client with heart failure taking digoxin refuses breakfast and reports nausea,
text: Question: A client with heart failure taking digoxin refuses breakfast and reports nausea, weakness, and blurred vision. What should the nurse do first?
A. Obtain current vital sign readings.
B. Obtain a prescription for a digoxin level.
C. Review the client’s current list of medications.
D. Request a prescription for an antiemetic.
Correct answer: A. Obtain current vital sign readings.
Topic: Pharmacology & Labs
notes: Rationale:
These are signs of digoxin toxicity (also visual halos, bradycardia, arrhythmias). Assess first, especially the apical pulse (hold if <60), then obtain a level and notify the provider.

slides.title: Which client should the nurse follow up with the PHCP?
text: Question: Which client should the nurse follow up with the PHCP?
A. Cushing’s disease prescribed fludrocortisone.
B. Potassium 6.2 mEq/L prescribed sodium polystyrene.
C. Aspirin sensitivity prescribed acetaminophen.
D. Penicillin rash prescribed an MAOI.
Correct answer: A. Cushing’s disease prescribed fludrocortisone.
Topic: Endocrine & Metabolic
notes: Rationale:
Fludrocortisone is a mineralocorticoid that retains sodium and water, which worsens the hypertension and fluid retention of Cushing’s disease. It is used in Addison’s disease.

slides.title: The nurse is preparing to teach a client with anemia and a new prescription for
text: Question: The nurse is preparing to teach a client with anemia and a new prescription for liquid ferrous sulfate. Which instruction is appropriate?
A. “Take the medication after dinner to avoid daytime drowsiness.”
B. “The medication can be taken with milk to prevent GI irritation.”
C. “Do not mix the medication with any other medications, foods, or liquids.”
D. “Eat plenty of iron-rich foods such as beans and green leafy vegetables.”
Correct answer: D. “Eat plenty of iron-rich foods such as beans and green leafy vegetables.”
Topic: Pharmacology & Labs
notes: Rationale:
Dietary iron supports therapy. Iron isn’t sedating, milk decreases absorption, and liquid iron is typically diluted and taken through a straw.

slides.title: A client receiving a continuous heparin infusion for PE. Which finding indicates
text: Question: A client receiving a continuous heparin infusion for PE. Which finding indicates an adverse effect?
A. PT 11.6 seconds
B. PTT 60 seconds
C. INR 3
D. Platelet count 90,000/mm³
Correct answer: D. Platelet count 90,000/mm³
Topic: Pharmacology & Labs
notes: Rationale:
Thrombocytopenia signals heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT): stop heparin and notify the provider. PTT 60 s is in the therapeutic range, and PT/INR monitor warfarin.

slides.title: A client who had abdominal surgery has these assessment data (PACU 1400 → floor
text: Question: A client who had abdominal surgery has these assessment data (PACU 1400 → floor 1415 → reassessment 1430): intraoperative blood loss 600 mL; dressing scant serous drainage; JP drain 5 mL; urine 60→50→40 mL/hr, BP 126/82→120/78→116/68, P 70→82→92, R 16→14→20, T 97.2° F, LR at 150 mL/hr. Which action should the nurse take?
A. Obtain a prescription for a bolus of IV fluids.
B. Irrigate the indwelling urinary catheter.
C. Continue to monitor the client.
D. Place the client on a warming blanket.
Correct answer: C. Continue to monitor the client.
Topic: Prioritization & Delegation
notes: Rationale:

Urine output stays above 30 mL/hr, vitals stay within normal limits, drainage is scant, and temperature is normal, so no intervention is needed. Continue monitoring the trends. (Your copy’s marked answer is C.)

slides.title: ABG: pH 7.52, PaCO₂ 38 mm Hg, HCO₃⁻ 30 mEq/L. Which imbalance?
text: Question: ABG: pH 7.52, PaCO₂ 38 mm Hg, HCO₃⁻ 30 mEq/L. Which imbalance?
A. Metabolic acidosis
B. Metabolic alkalosis
C. Respiratory acidosis
D. Respiratory alkalosis
Correct answer: B. Metabolic alkalosis
Topic: Renal, Fluids & Acid-Base
notes: Rationale:
High pH with high bicarbonate and normal CO₂ = metabolic alkalosis (normal pH 7.35–7.45, CO₂ 35–45, HCO₃ 22–26).

slides.title: A client with type 1 diabetes is taught about exercise. Which statement shows un
text: Question: A client with type 1 diabetes is taught about exercise. Which statement shows understanding?
A. “I will start my exercise near the time my insulin peaks.”
B. “I will eat a carbohydrate snack after exercising if it will be more than 1 hour before my next meal.”
C. “I will carry a complex sugar when exercising.”
D. “I will avoid exercising if my blood glucose is less than 100.”
Correct answer: B. “I will eat a carbohydrate snack after exercising if it will be more than 1 hour before my next meal.”
Topic: Endocrine & Metabolic
notes: Rationale:
Exercise lowers glucose for hours; eat a carbohydrate snack to prevent delayed hypoglycemia. Avoid exercising at insulin peak and carry fast-acting simple sugar.

slides.title: Which statement shows correct understanding of collecting a midstream urine spec
text: Question: Which statement shows correct understanding of collecting a midstream urine specimen (female client)?
A. “Since I’m right-handed, I’ll use my left hand to spread the labia apart.”
B. “I will use the towelette to cleanse using a back-and-forth motion.”
C. “I will urinate in the container and then finish urinating in the toilet.”
D. “I will hold the specimen container against my skin while collecting.”
Correct answer: A. “Since I’m right-handed, I’ll use my left hand to spread the labia apart.”
Topic: Skills & Procedures
notes: Rationale:

Spread the labia with the non-dominant hand and keep the dominant hand free for the container. Cleanse front to back, start the stream in the toilet, then collect midstream without touching the container to the skin.

slides.title: A client with lung cancer receives external radiation. Which statement shows a n
text: Question: A client with lung cancer receives external radiation. Which statement shows a need for further teaching?
A. “I will use a washcloth with antibacterial soap and water to cleanse the radiation area every day.”
B. “I will prevent direct sun exposure during treatment and for at least 1 year.”
C. “I should avoid moisturizers, creams, lotions, or powders on the radiation area unless prescribed.”
D. “It will be safe for me to be around my pregnant daughter and grandchildren.”
Correct answer: A. “I will use a washcloth with antibacterial soap and water to cleanse the radiation area every day.”
Topic: Oncology & Radiation
notes: Rationale:
Use only mild soap and lukewarm water with the hand (no washcloth, no friction), pat dry, and do not scrub off the markings. External beam radiation does not make the client radioactive.

slides.title: A client in the ED is bleeding heavily from a deep forearm laceration. After app
text: Question: A client in the ED is bleeding heavily from a deep forearm laceration. After applying direct pressure, which action should the nurse take next?
A. Perform a comprehensive head-to-toe assessment.
B. Insert a large-bore IV catheter.
C. Cleanse the wound with normal saline.
D. Prepare the client for suturing.
Correct answer: B. Insert a large-bore IV catheter.
Topic: Burns, Trauma & Emergencies
notes: Rationale:
Circulation: control the bleeding, then establish IV access for fluid/blood replacement. Cleaning and suturing happen after hemodynamic stability.

slides.title: Which manifestations should the nurse monitor for peritonitis in a client receiv
text: Question: Which manifestations should the nurse monitor for peritonitis in a client receiving peritoneal dialysis?
A. Hyperactive bowel sounds.
B. Nausea and vomiting.
C. Increased amylase level.
D. Burgundy-colored urine.
Correct answer: B. Nausea and vomiting.
Topic: GI & Nutrition
notes: Rationale:
Peritonitis: abdominal pain, cloudy outflow, fever, N/V, and decreased bowel sounds. Hyperactive bowel sounds and amylase are not typical.

slides.title: A client has type 1 diabetes, blood glucose >600, and HHS. Which finding should
text: Question: A client has type 1 diabetes, blood glucose >600, and HHS. Which finding should the nurse expect?
A. Positive urine ketones.
B. Fluid volume deficit.
C. Serum pH less than 7.35.
D. Kussmaul respirations.
Correct answer: B. Fluid volume deficit.
Topic: Endocrine & Metabolic
notes: Rationale:
HHS causes profound osmotic diuresis → severe dehydration. Ketosis/acidosis/Kussmaul respirations are DKA findings (HHS has enough insulin to prevent ketones).

slides.title: A visitor in the hospital cafeteria begins to cough and signals that they are ch
text: Question: A visitor in the hospital cafeteria begins to cough and signals that they are choking. What should the nurse do first?
A. Begin CPR.
B. Call for assistance.
C. Prepare to deliver abdominal thrusts.
D. Open the airway and attempt to ventilate.
Correct answer: C. Prepare to deliver abdominal thrusts.
Topic: Burns, Trauma & Emergencies
notes: Rationale:
A conscious choking adult with an obstructed airway needs abdominal thrusts immediately. CPR is for an unresponsive victim.

slides.title: A client in labor has persistent late decelerations with 50% or more of contract
text: Question: A client in labor has persistent late decelerations with 50% or more of contractions. The nurse interprets this as
A. uteroplacental insufficiency.
B. maternal bradycardia.
C. umbilical cord compression.
D. fetal head compression.
Correct answer: A. uteroplacental insufficiency.
Topic: Maternal-Newborn
notes: Rationale:
Late decels = uteroplacental insufficiency (VELCRO: Variable–cord compression, Early–head compression, Late–placental insufficiency). Turn left, give O₂, stop oxytocin, and notify.
